title: Is the ceiling area safe for passenger use?
prompt: Has facilities/engineering confirmed the main entrance ceiling zone is safe to open?
whyItMatters: Reopening the main entrance without confirmation could create safety and reputational risk.

title: Can the side entrance safely handle early morning passenger flow?
prompt: Is side entrance staffing, barriers and wayfinding sufficient for the peak?
whyItMatters: Passenger safety and queue management depend on a viable alternate route.

title: Are train services affected?
prompt: Is any train service change required or planned?
whyItMatters: Public lines must distinguish station access from train service.
resolutionNote: NOC confirmation recorded from duty overnight pack (operational report ~04:55).

title: What public line should be used if asked whether the station is shut?
prompt: What wording distinguishes main entrance closure from whole-station closure?
whyItMatters: Social posts and passenger confusion create reputational risk.
resolutionNote: Approved passenger, social and holding press lines in use from 05:52–06:18 — distinguishes main entrance closure from whole-station closure.

title: What is the expected main entrance reopening time?
prompt: When can we commit to reopening the main entrance?
whyItMatters: Press and passenger messaging need a realistic time window.
resolutionNote: Working estimate ~08:00 in updated passenger message from 07:22; main entrance confirmed open 08:12.

title: Are accessibility arrangements adequate while the main entrance is closed?
prompt: Is step-free access clearly signed and operationally supported?
whyItMatters: Accessibility must be verified independently of general passenger flow.
resolutionNote: Accessibility assessment logged in Metis; temporary signage improvements still being deployed (action required).

title: What follow-up action is needed before future planned works?
prompt: What handback criteria, signage and pre-agreed passenger messaging should be updated?
whyItMatters: Executive request for learning and prevention.
